title: Proper tame-pair generators for finite-field constructible complexes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extended $\ell$-adic norm topology. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix a finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. Put $A_E(S)=C(S,E)$ on profinite sets with its norm topology [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and $A_{E,T}=p_T^*A_E$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal module objects, ordinary unbounded derived module categories and their derived direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Constructible means finite constant local models on finite constructible stratifications [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

A pair used below consists of a regular scheme $Y$ [def-weil-regular-scheme], a reduced strict normal crossings boundary $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ with finitely many components [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], a subset $A_{\rm out}\subseteq A$, and the open immersions $j':V=Y\setminus\bigcup_{a\in A_{\rm out}}D_a\hookrightarrow Y$, $b:W=Y\setminus D\hookrightarrow V$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. The empty divisor and empty subset are allowed. A finite-rank lisse $A_{E,W}$-module $L$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] is called tame along $D$ here precisely when the following local condition holds: at every geometric point of $Y$, take the strict henselization and regular parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ cutting out the components of $D$ through that point; the restriction of $L$ to the complement of $t_1\cdots t_r=0$ becomes constant on the inverse-limit cover obtained by adjoining compatible $n$th roots of all $t_i$ for all positive integers $n$ prime to $p$. This condition is imposed on the pulled-back pro-etale module, and is independent of the chosen parameters. For $r=0$ the cover is the identity. All open immersions here are quasi-compact, since these schemes are Noetherian.

Fix a quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. Consider all diagrams with $p:Y\to X$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], $V=p^{-1}(U)$, $q=p|_V:V\to U$ proper, and a pair $(Y,D,A_{\rm out},W,L)$ as above whose $V$ is this inverse image. Put $G=Rq_{*,A_E}(b_!L)[0]$, where $b_!$ is exact open extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. Then every $C\in\Dbc(U,A_E)$ belongs to the thick subcategory generated by these $G$: it is obtained, up to isomorphism, by finitely many shifts, finite sums, distinguished-triangle cones and retracts from finitely many such $G$ and zero. A retract means maps $C\xrightarrow{i}H\xrightarrow{r}C$ with $ri=1_C$; no infinite coproducts or infinite totalizations are allowed [def-weil-triangulated-category]. This is a finite-$E$ generation assertion, with no scalar extension to $B$ in its conclusion.

source.place: Agent-stated finite-E generation input motivated by IX Theorem 1.1 and XIII 2.2.2; the exact finite thick-generation and tame-coefficient assertion is WANTED, not quoted as an ILO theorem.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal H\subset D(U,A_E)$ be the full thick subcategory generated by the stated proper tame-pair objects. By det-lem-integral-models-generators(1), it suffices to put $(a_!M_0)[1/\ell]$ in $\mathcal H$ for every locally closed $a:S\hookrightarrow U$ and lisse integral lattice $M_0$. The extension/scalar formula det-lem-integral-models-operations(4) identifies this object with $a_!M$, $M=M_0[1/\ell]$. The functor $a_!$ here has the exact, factorization-independent meaning of lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence; thus the same notation may be used after subdividing a stratum. Throughout, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence identifies internal modules with the sectionwise modules over the same ring sheaf, preserving underlying sheaves and actions. Apply this exact equivalence and its inverse termwise to transport the cited sheaf-module localization and composition statements to the internal module-derived categories.

source.place: 6.8.13-6.8.14; existing integral-model generation and scalar/extension formula

proof.text: We prove, by Noetherian induction on closed subsets $Z\subseteq U$, that every bounded constructible complex on $U$ with zero restriction to $U\setminus Z$ belongs to $\mathcal H$. This induction is valid by lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal. The empty support gives zero by the closed support identification in lem-sfb-condensed-support-derived-localization. In the inductive step all proper closed subsets of $Z$ are assumed, for every bounded constructible complex supported on them, rather than only for sheaves. Realize $Z$ as its reduced induced closed subscheme; localization identifies a supported complex with the exact closed direct image of its restriction to $Z$. Restrictions preserve its finite scalar local models simply by pulling back their covers and stratifications. Closed extension preserves these models by lem-sfb-scalar-model-immersion-extension. Apply step 1 on $Z$ and then this exact closed extension. We are reduced to $a_!M$ with the closure of $S$ contained in $Z$; if that closure is proper the induction hypothesis already applies.

We may reduce these strata to integral ones. There are finitely many irreducible components by lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components. The complement of the pairwise intersections is a disjoint union of dense opens of those components. Replace each such open by its reduction: its map to the original open is a universal homeomorphism, so lem-trf-proetale-topological-invariance and the Cartesian coefficient isomorphisms identify their module categories, lattices, and exact extensions. The open/closed short exact sequence of lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed, and its triangle from lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle, separate these finitely many pieces from the remaining proper closed subset. Apply the inductive hypothesis to the latter. Thus it remains to treat an integral $S$ whose reduced closure $T$ in $X$ meets $U$ in an integral closed subscheme $T^\circ=T\cap U$, with $S$ dense open in $T^\circ$. Its inclusion in $U$ is still $a$. All assertions are about reduced closed structures, so no regularity of $X$, $T$, or $S$ has been assumed.

Apply lem-sfb-lisse-lattice-potential-kummer-tameness to $M_0$ on this connected $S$, obtaining $c:H\to S$. Apply lem-sfb-nested-open-regular-alteration to $S\subseteq T^\circ\subseteq T$ and $c$. Write $h:Y\to T$, $W=h^{-1}S$, $V=h^{-1}T^\circ$, $r:W\to S$, and $S_0\subset S$ for its data. Compose $h$ with the closed immersion $T\hookrightarrow X$ to obtain $p:Y\to X$. A closed immersion is proper, and proper maps compose; hence $p$ is proper and $p^{-1}U=V$. Its restriction $q:V\to U$ is proper by base change. These statements use no separability of the generic extension. The reduced boundary and the selected outer components are exactly those of the geometric input.

source.place: X Theorem 2.1, p.149; adapted nested-boundary alteration

proof.text:
Set $L=r^*M$ on $W$. Exact Cartesian pullback preserves the given finite free local trivializations, so $L$ is lisse over $A_{E,W}$. Since $r$ factors through $H$, lem-sfb-lisse-lattice-potential-kummer-tameness says that $L$ satisfies precisely the parameter-root tameness condition of the item, for every parameter choice, including points with no boundary. Thus
$$G=Rq_*(b_!L)[0]$$
is one of the generators of $\mathcal H$. Moreover $b_!L$ is bounded constructible by lem-sfb-scalar-model-immersion-extension, and $G$ is bounded constructible by det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational(2), used only for the finite field $E$. These boundedness and constructibility assertions will be needed for the error terms of the induction.

source.place: 6.8.4 and 6.8.15; finite-E proper direct image only

proof.text: Put $r_0:W_0\to S_0$ as in the geometric input and $M'=M|_{S_0}$. Its factorization $W_0\xrightarrow{u}T_0\xrightarrow{e}S_0$ has a finite universal homeomorphism followed by a degree-$d$ finite etale surjection. The equivalence in lem-trf-proetale-topological-invariance lifts to internal coefficient modules by sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients: apply the quasi-inverse functors to the action and its axioms, using the coefficient identification. Therefore $u_*$ is exact and its unit identifies $u_*u^*e^*M'$ with $e^*M'$. On each etale splitting of $e$ supplied by lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split, the unit into $e_*e^*M'$ is the diagonal into $d$ copies. The sum of the copies is invariant under permutation of the sheets, hence glues on overlaps to an $A_{E,S_0}$-linear trace. The local product description also shows $e_*$ exact. Thus $Rr_{0*}r_0^*M'=r_{0*}r_0^*M'$ in degree zero and the trace composed with the unit is $d\,1_{M'}$. Multiplication by $1/d\in E$ gives a retraction. We divide by the separable degree $d\geq1$, not by a possibly inseparable field trace.

The map $r:W\to S$ is proper. The map $W\hookrightarrow V$ followed by $V\to T^\circ$ is a dense compactification of $W\xrightarrow{r}S\hookrightarrow T^\circ$. Apply det-sf-comp-composition-interchange(3) to the bounded constructible input $L[0]$ (it has Tor amplitude zero since it is locally free). Composing with exact closed direct image $T^\circ\hookrightarrow U$ and the canonical derived direct-image composition comparison yields
$$G\simeq a_!Rr_*L.$$
Exactness, mixed-factorization independence, and composition of these locally closed extensions are supplied by lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence. In particular $G$ has zero restriction outside the closure of $S$ in $U$, which is $Z$. Open restriction to $S_0$ is proper base change, clause (3) of det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational. Under it $G|_{S_0}\simeq Rr_{0*}r_0^*M'$. No assertion about an SNC boundary for $W_0$ was needed.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), through the cited finite-E interchange statement

proof.text:
Let $v:S_0\hookrightarrow S$ be the open immersion and $z:B=S\setminus S_0\hookrightarrow S$ its reduced closed complement. Write $N=Rr_*L\in\Dbc(S,A_E)$, by proper rational finiteness. Apply the open/closed triangle to $N$, and then exact $a_!$:
$$ (av)_!v^*N\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow a_!z_*z^*N\longrightarrow (av)_!v^*N[1].$$
This triangle comes by applying the termwise exact open/closed sequence to a representative complex, using det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf and lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle; exact a_! preserves this triangle by lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated. Its third term is bounded constructible, since exact restrictions preserve local scalar models and locally closed extension preserves them. Its support is contained in the closure of $B$ in $U$, a proper closed subset of $Z$: $S_0$ is nonempty open dense in integral $Z$, and $B\subset Z\setminus S_0$. The inductive hypothesis puts that third term in $\mathcal H$. The middle term is its generator $G$, so closure under cones and shifts puts $(av)_!v^*N$ in $\mathcal H$.

source.place: Tag 09AH; finite support-error triangle after generic shrinking

proof.text:
Apply exact $(av)_!$ to the unit and the $1/d$-normalized trace in step 6. With the open restriction identification of step 7 this exhibits $(av)_!M'$ as a retract of $(av)_!v^*N$. Hence $(av)_!M'\in\mathcal H$. Apply the same open/closed triangle on $S$ to $M[0]$, then $a_!$:
$$ (av)_!M'\longrightarrow a_!M\longrightarrow a_!z_*z^*M\longrightarrow (av)_!M'[1].$$
The last nonshifted term is bounded constructible and supported on the same proper closed subset of $Z$, so belongs to $\mathcal H$ by induction. The first term belongs by the explicit retract. Thus $a_!M\in\mathcal H$. This completes the inductive step and then step 1 gives every $C\in\Dbc(U,A_E)$. Each induction call removes a proper closed support, valid by the stated Noetherian induction principle; each branch uses finitely many lattice generators and cones. The resulting expression therefore uses finitely many generators, shifts, sums, cones and retracts, and never an infinite totalization or scalar extension beyond $E$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NS-630714a40 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: First split of lem-sfb-tame-pair-proper-generators (no re-split note; item, new nodes not in route-pivot-dropped; item still unsplit live; statement unchanged, no SGA). The 9 steps are correct: step 1 generates from integral lattices (det-lem-integral-models-generators(1) and -operations(4)); steps 2-3 run Noetherian support induction with a reduction to integral S dense open in T°=Z; in step 4 p=(T↪X)∘h is proper and p^{-1}U=V; step 5 makes L=r^*M tame through H, with b_!L and G in D^b_c (rational proper (2)); in step 6 u is a universal homeomorphism (equivalence) and e is finite étale of degree d with trace/d, so 1/d∈E even if ℓ|d; step 7 is det-sf-comp-composition-interchange(3) with p=r, i=S↪T° and compactification W↪V→T° dense, input L[0]∈Dctf, cartesian square, giving G≅a_!Rr_*L; steps 8-9 are the two open/closed error triangles supported on cl(S∖S_0), which is proper in integral Z, plus the retract. New lem-sfb-nested-open-regular-alteration is true. I checked it against ILO X Thm 2.1 p.149 and proof 2.3 (smooth X̃/k', SNC preimage). Cartier blowups make T∖T° a union of components. The compactified component of H restricts to itself over S. Using the separable subextension (030K), shrinking gives a universal homeomorphism followed by a finite étale map of degree d≥1. New lem-sfb-lisse-lattice-potential-kummer-tameness is true: after trivializing mod ϖ the monodromy lies in a pro-ℓ congruence kernel, the wild pro-p part dies, ℓ-covers are Kummer-split on the prime-to-p root tower (Abhyankar/purity, ILO IX 2.1), and BS 6.8.4 reconstructs the lattice. Neither new node duplicates an existing one: the per snc/gabber-cover nodes differ and are dropped. Neither restates the item.
